title: Mukesh Kumar takes 4 for 9 as Bengal crush Chandigarh; IPL retention deadline is today
dek: Bengal won by 85 runs in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, and Hyderabad edged Chhattisgarh by one wicket at Eden Gardens. Franchises must name their retained players by Tuesday.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Mukesh Kumar took four wickets for nine runs, the best figures of his T20 career, as Bengal beat Chandigarh by 85 runs at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai on Monday in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, the national T20 championship. The win came on a day of lopsided results across the tournament, as IPL franchises prepared to submit their lists of retained and released players by Tuesday's deadline.

## How Bengal won

Wicketkeeper-batter Abishek Porel made 53 off 26 balls and Rishabh Chaudhary 33 off 19 as Bengal reached 200 for 7 in their 20 overs. In reply, Mukesh, the India seamer, took 4 for 9, Karan Lal took 3 for 24, and Chandigarh were all out for 115 in 15.5 overs, according to reports.

In Kolkata, Eden Gardens hosted the closest match of the day, in which Hyderabad beat Chhattisgarh by one wicket chasing 169. Hyderabad slumped to 129 for 7, and after Rahul Buddhi (28) and Tanay Thyagarajan (19) kept the chase alive, the last-wicket pair of Ajay Dev Goud, who had earlier taken 4 for 28, and Rakshan Readdi took them home.

## Elsewhere

- In Indore, Delhi made 240, with Yash Dhull unbeaten on 78 off 40 balls and Priyansh Arya scoring 55 off 32, and then bowled Punjab out to win by 109 runs. Fast bowler Mayank Yadav took 4 for 12, including a triple-wicket maiden.
- In New Chandigarh, Kerala made 211 for 8, with Rohan Kunnummal scoring 75 off 47 and Sanju Samson 47 off 16, and bowled Maharashtra out for 117 to win by 94 runs. M.D. Nidheesh took 5 for 27 and was player of the match.
- Rajasthan beat the defending champions Jharkhand by 55 runs, Vidarbha beat Odisha by eight wickets, Himachal Pradesh beat Andhra by eight runs and Bihar beat Railways by four wickets, according to reports.

## IPL retention deadline

The 10 IPL franchises must submit their retention and release lists for the 2027 season by Tuesday, 17 November, after the deadline was moved back from 15 November, according to reports. Player registration for the auction closes on 23 November, and the auction is scheduled for 16 December.

The last trades are being completed before the deadline. Lucknow Super Giants are set to trade fast bowler Mohammed Shami to Rajasthan Royals in exchange for England all-rounder Sam Curran, according to reports on Monday; neither franchise nor the IPL had confirmed the deal by Tuesday morning. Earlier this month the IPL confirmed the trade of Hardik Pandya from Mumbai Indians to Punjab Kings for Rs 18 crore, with Arshdeep Singh moving the other way at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore.

## What's next

India's men begin their Test series against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday, 19 November, after winning the one-day series 3-1. The Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy group stage continues through the week.
